ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Pregnancy changes ulcer prevention

A woman taking naproxen is evaluated for gastric ulcer prophylaxis. She has missed a menstrual period and has a positive pregnancy test. Which property of misoprostol makes it inappropriate for this ulcer-prevention indication?

  1. It causes fetal ototoxicity through aminoglycoside activity
  2. It blocks maternal thyroid hormone synthesis
  3. It prevents intestinal folate absorption by chelation
  4. It can stimulate uterine contractions and pregnancy loss
  5. It irreversibly inhibits platelet aggregation
Answer and explanation

It can stimulate uterine contractions and pregnancy loss

Misoprostol must not be used for NSAID-ulcer prevention during pregnancy because of uterotonic and pregnancy-related risks.

Option explanations

It can stimulate uterine contractions and pregnancy loss: Misoprostol must not be used for NSAID-ulcer prevention during pregnancy because of uterotonic and pregnancy-related risks.

It irreversibly inhibits platelet aggregation: It is not an irreversible platelet inhibitor.

It causes fetal ototoxicity through aminoglycoside activity: It is not an aminoglycoside.

It blocks maternal thyroid hormone synthesis: It does not inhibit thyroid hormone synthesis.

It prevents intestinal folate absorption by chelation: Its principal pregnancy warning is not folate chelation.
